name: Question 12
problem:
$$ \{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}=0.8x-0.4xy \\ {y}^{′}=-0.3y+1.2xy\end{aligned} $$ Consider the Lotka-Volterra model above, where $x=x(t)$ represents the prey and $y=y(t)$ represents the predators. Select the correct options in the reasoning below.$\,$ Evaluating the Jacobian of the system at the equilibrium ${x}^{∗}=[0.25,\,2]^{T},$ we get
$J({x}^{∗})=\,\,$ {{field-1}} {{field-2}} $\,.$
{{field-3}} {{field-4}}
$\,$ The eigenvalues of the Jacobian matrix are {{field-5}}. $\,$ Therefore, the equilibrium at ${x}^{∗}$ is {{field-6}}{{field-7}}.
worked_solution:
Let's denote ${f}_{1}(x,y)=0.8x-0.4xy$ and ${f}_{2}(x,y)=-0.3y+1.2xy.$

Now, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(0.8x-0.4xy)=0.8-0.4y,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(0.8x-0.4xy)=-0.4x \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-0.3y+1.2xy)=1.2y,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(-0.3y+1.2xy)=-0.3+1.2x\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the Jacobian matrix is

$$
J=[\begin{aligned}0.8-0.4y & -0.4x \\ 1.2y & -0.3+1.2x\end{aligned}].
$$

Next, we evaluate the Jacobian at the equilibrium ${x}^{∗}=[\begin{aligned}0.25 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ to get

$$
J({x}^{∗})=[\begin{aligned}0.8-0.4(2) & -0.4(0.25) \\ 1.2(2) & -0.3+1.2(0.25)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & -0.1 \\ 2.4 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the eigenvalues of the Jacobian matrix, we write down the characteristic equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}-\lambda  & -0.1 \\ 2.4 & -\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-\lambda )(-\lambda )-2.4\cdot (-0.1) & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}+0.24 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the equation, we get the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1,2}=\pm 0.2\sqrt{6}\,\text{i}.$ Since the eigenvalues are purely imaginary, our equilibrium is $\text{a stable}$ $\text{center}.$

**Note:**
For the Lotka-Volterra model (as in this problem), it is safe to classify the nonzero equilibrium as a center when the linearization has purely imaginary eigenvalues. 

**Watch out!** 
In contrast, for a general nonlinear system, the Jacobian test alone is inconclusive (additional analysis is required to determine whether the equilibrium is a true center or a spiral sink/source).

EXPLANATION

Let's denote f1(x,y)=0.8x−0.4xy and f2(x,y)=−0.3y+1.2xy.

Now, we compute the partial derivatives:

∂f1∂x=∂∂x(0.8x−0.4xy)=0.8−0.4y,∂f1∂y=∂∂y(0.8x−0.4xy)=−0.4x∂f2∂x=∂∂x(−0.3y+1.2xy)=1.2y,∂f2∂y=∂∂y(−0.3y+1.2xy)=−0.3+1.2x

Thus, the Jacobian matrix is J=[0.8−0.4y−0.4x1.2y−0.3+1.2x].

Next, we evaluate the Jacobian at the equilibrium x∗=[0.252] to get

J(x∗)=[0.8−0.4(2)−0.4(0.25)1.2(2)−0.3+1.2(0.25)]=[0−0.12.40].

To find the eigenvalues of the Jacobian matrix, we write down the characteristic equation:

|−λ−0.12.4−λ|=0(−λ)(−λ)−2.4⋅(−0.1)=0λ2+0.24=0

Solving the equation, we get the eigenvalues λ1,2=±0.26i. Since the eigenvalues are purely imaginary, our equilibrium is a stable center.

Note: For the Lotka-Volterra model (as in this problem), it is safe to classify the nonzero equilibrium as a center when the linearization has purely imaginary eigenvalues.

Watch out! In contrast, for a general nonlinear system, the Jacobian test alone is inconclusive (additional analysis is required to determine whether the equilibrium is a true center or a spiral sink/source).
